extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom style guide providing terminology, usage guidance, sensitivities, and preferred alternatives for reporting on race/ethnicity, disability, religion, gender, sexuality, immigration, and related topics. Entries explain preferred terms, words to avoid, capitalization notes, and reporting tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: "bathroom bill"
rubrics_metrics.description: An inaccurate phrase created and used by far-right extremists to oppose nondiscrimination laws that protect transgender people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the phrase; it is meant to incite fear. Refer instead to the nondiscrimination law/ordinance. See GLAAD guidance on accurate reporting on nondiscrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: "broken family," "broken home"
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms that carry judgment and suggest that the family needs to be fixed and are disproportionately applied to Black families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternatives such as divorced parents, parents living apart, single-parent households, etc., and use these terms with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: "circle the wagons"
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase meaning 'to become defensive' or to confer only within a trusted group; may be offensive to some Indigenous people due to colonial-era associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the phrase's historical connotations and avoid usage when it may offend; provide context or choose different phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Don’t ask, don’t tell"
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorthand for the U.S. military's former policy (1993–2011) forbidding inquiry about service members' sexual orientation and prohibiting disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to the policy, clarify the full name and years; use accurate background for historical reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: "ex-gay"
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to the movement that aims to change a person’s sexual orientation; widely discredited by scientific communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid endorsing the term; consult GLAAD Media Reference Guide on conversion therapy and 'ex-gays'.

rubrics_metrics.name: "school-to-prison pipeline"
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and practices that push schoolchildren, especially at-risk children, out of classrooms and into juvenile and criminal justice systems (ACLU definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the term, explain the policies/practices involved and cite authoritative sources such as the ACLU.

rubrics_metrics.name: "separate but equal"
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal doctrine from Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) that allowed segregation if facilities were ostensibly equal; historically led to Jim Crow laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context and explain true inequities between segregated services when reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: "White Man's Burden"
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to Rudyard Kipling's 1899 poem promoting colonialist notions and the American role in the Philippines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When quoting or referencing, consider including full text or historical context and avoid uncritical use of the phrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: (partial) hearing loss/partially deaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on terminology for people with mild to moderate hearing loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'hard of hearing' as the most common and generally acceptable term; ask the individual their preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: #BlackoutDay, #TheBlackout
rubrics_metrics.description: A social media campaign to celebrate Black history and the beauty of Black people, encouraging photo sharing with specified hashtags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include background on origins, organizers, dates, and purpose when reporting; attribute founders and movement rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.D.
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviation for anno Domini; traditionally used to date years after the birth of Jesus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP style remains A.D. and B.C.; use A.D. preceding the year (e.g., A.D. 77). Note increasing scholarly use of B.C.E./C.E.

rubrics_metrics.name: abaya
rubrics_metrics.description: A robelike garment worn by some Muslim women, often black and sometimes worn with a hijab or niqab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe accurately; note possible combinations with hijab or niqab and avoid stereotyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABC
rubrics_metrics.description: Slang for 'American-Born Chinese,' often referring to U.S.-born people of Chinese descent; may imply cultural disconnection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize nuance and avoid using the label carelessly; consider context and preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABCD
rubrics_metrics.description: Short for 'American Born Confused Desi'; many consider it a slur referring to children of Indian immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid casual use; be cautious as it echoes derogatory terms applied to immigrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: able-bodied
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to describe someone who does not identify as having a disability; some oppose the term as implying all people with disabilities lack ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'non-disabled' or 'does not have a disability' for neutrality; 'able-bodied' acceptable in some contexts like workforce statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ableism
rubrics_metrics.description: Prejudiced thoughts, attitudes, or discriminatory actions based on differences in physical, mental, or emotional ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term to describe systemic or interpersonal discrimination; alternatives include 'disability discrimination' or 'disability oppression.'

rubrics_metrics.name: abnormal/abnormality
rubrics_metrics.description: Term meaning deviation from normal; acceptable in medical/scientific contexts but derogatory when applied to people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'abnormal' to describe a person; prefer specific medical descriptions; use 'typical' instead of 'normal' when contrasting abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: abolition
rubrics_metrics.description: Historic American reform movement to end slavery; includes contributions from African American leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, include diverse historical actors and avoid simplistic portrayals that center only white abolitionists.

rubrics_metrics.name: abortion
rubrics_metrics.description: A nuanced issue; reporters should describe people's views precisely rather than using polarized labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'pro-abortion rights' instead of 'pro-choice' and 'opposed to abortion' or 'against abortion rights' instead of 'pro-life'; follow AP guidance using 'anti-abortion' and 'abortion rights' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: accents and direct quotation of
rubrics_metrics.description: See dialect (entry cross-reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use guidance under 'dialect' for handling accents and quoting speech in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: accessibility, accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunity to access programs, services and facilities for people with disabilities; extent to which a facility is usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'accessible' to describe usability; consider physical and programmatic accessibility when reporting on spaces and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: acting, appearing (gay, straight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases that make judgmental assumptions about a subject’s sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid such phrases; they assume authenticity of orientation and are generally discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: activist, advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between someone actively pushing for change (activist) and the more neutral term advocate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'advocate' in news copy unless a subject self-identifies as an activist or context requires 'activist.'

rubrics_metrics.name: addict, addiction
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Addiction' defined as a neurobiological disease; 'addict' is stigmatizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use people-first language: 'someone experiencing a drug/alcohol problem' or 'someone with an addiction.' Avoid 'junkie', 'clean/dirty' for drug tests; say 'tested positive for (drug)'. Use 'recovering' or 'in recovery' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: adhan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Islamic call to prayer (chanted in Arabic by a mu’adin or muezzin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what the adhan is and note that wording and practice vary by country and branch of Islam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adi Granth
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sikh holy book (also Guru Granth Sahib), considered the 11th and lasting guru.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pronunciation guidance and context about placement in gurdwaras and its status in Sikhism.

rubrics_metrics.name: adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Language around adoption has evolved; many older terms are now inaccurate/offensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention adoption only if relevant, use past-tense ('was adopted'), refer to parents as 'father/mother' rather than 'real/natural parents,' avoid 'abandoned' or 'given up,' avoid calling children 'orphans' if birth parents are alive, and avoid portraying adoptive parents as unusually saintly.

rubrics_metrics.name: adultism
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors and attitudes assuming adults are better than young people and entitled to act upon them without agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term to describe institutional and attitudinal mistreatment of youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: affirmative action
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy measures to address discrimination in employment, education and contracting originating under the Civil Rights Act era; subject to litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context, avoid myths (e.g., that African Americans are chief beneficiaries), and cite authoritative sources when explaining impacts and beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: afflicted with/stricken with/suffers from/victim of
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrasing that assumes a person with a disability is suffering or has reduced quality of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer neutral language stating the nature of the disability; e.g., 'He has muscular dystrophy.' Avoid presuming suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Africa
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical and regional definitions including sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa; cautions about using 'Black Africa'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'Black Africa'; when relevant, specify subregions and list countries; be precise and avoid politically incorrect labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: African American, African-American, Black, black
rubrics_metrics.description: People in the U.S. with lineage traceable to Africa; both 'African American' and 'Black' are generally acceptable but may differ in meaning and preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask individuals their preference; if not possible, using either term is acceptable. Use 'Black people' rather than 'Blacks' in text; 'Blacks' may be acceptable in headlines. Discuss capitalization (many guides now capitalize 'Black'); provide historical context about terminology evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: African diaspora
rubrics_metrics.description: Black people of African descent scattered globally as a result of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade and later migrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the term, provide historical context and definitions from authoritative sources like the National Association of Black Journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: African Methodist Episcopal Zion / African Methodist Episcopal (AME)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and denominational descriptions of AME Zion and AME churches, including origins and naming conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'AME' or 'AME Zion Church' appropriately; note acceptable second-reference forms and historical details when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afro-American
rubrics_metrics.description: An archaic term for Black people; was popular in the 1960s–70s and later replaced by 'Black' and 'African American'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use; refer to 'African American' or 'Black' per preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afrocentric, Afrocentrism
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of Africa and its history from a non-European perspective aiming to restore Africa’s historical place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define term and its origin (Molefi Kete Asante, 1976) and use descriptively rather than pejoratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: ageism
rubrics_metrics.description: Stereotyping and prejudice based on age, often directed toward older people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term to describe discriminatory attitudes and institutional practices; provide definition and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: agender
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who identifies as neither male nor female.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask individuals about pronoun preference; cross-reference related terms such as non-binary and genderqueer.

rubrics_metrics.name: aging
rubrics_metrics.description: An ongoing, all-inclusive process rather than a label for older, frail adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pejorative or reductive language; describe processes and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: aging in place
rubrics_metrics.description: The concept of people remaining in their homes despite physical or mental decline, preserving social networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When covering, note design, accessibility, services, and community features that enable aging in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: agnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone unsure whether there is a God or who believes God's existence is unknowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate agnostic from atheist and use accurately in religious reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alaska Native
rubrics_metrics.description: Umbrella term including Inupiat, Yupik, Alaskan Indians (Athabascan, Haida, Tlingit, Tsimshian) and Aleut; preferred over a generic grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask individuals or community leaders for preference; use specific tribal affiliation when possible. Note controversy over 'Eskimo' and advise caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: alcoholic, alcoholism
rubrics_metrics.description: Alcoholism is characterized as a disease; 'alcoholic' can be stigmatizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use people-first language: 'someone with alcoholism' or 'someone with an alcohol problem'; use 'recovering' for people overcoming addiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcoholics Anonymous
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship founded in 1935; anonymity is central to the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose membership only when essential; consider using first names only unless official references require otherwise. Apply similar caution to other 12-step programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: alien
rubrics_metrics.description: Term historically used by the U.S. government for foreign-born noncitizens; now considered pejorative by many immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'alien' and 'illegal alien' in favor of 'noncitizen', 'undocumented noncitizen', or 'undocumented individual' per recent DHS guidance (Feb 2021). Use 'alien' only in historical or legal contexts with attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alien Land Laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Early 1900s laws in Western states preventing Asians from owning land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, explain historical repeal and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-American
rubrics_metrics.description: Term referring to top athletes and not a synonym for white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution and do not use as a racial descriptor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allah
rubrics_metrics.description: Arabic word for God; some Muslims prefer 'God' when addressing non-Muslims, but 'Allah' should be used when quoting text or persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Allah' when quoting or when the context warrants; otherwise 'God' may be used with sensitivity to sources' preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allahu akbar
rubrics_metrics.description: Arabic phrase meaning 'God is great' or 'God is the greatest', used in prayer and as exclamation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain meaning and common contexts; avoid implying violent connotations without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: ally
rubrics_metrics.description: A person committed to recognizing privilege and working in solidarity with oppressed groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define allyship as active commitment, awareness, and ongoing learning; avoid labeling without evidence of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alzheimer's disease
rubrics_metrics.description: Progressive fatal neurodegenerative disease; proper term is 'Alzheimer's disease' (not 'Alzheimer's').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose diagnosis only if relevant and formally diagnosed; use 'person who has Alzheimer's disease' rather than 'suffers from/afflicted with.'

rubrics_metrics.name: America / American
rubrics_metrics.description: 'América' geography vs. United States: 'America' refers to the Western hemisphere; 'American' commonly refers to U.S. residents but may be seen as imperialist by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to the U.S., use 'United States', 'U.S.', or 'U.S.A.' where clarity is needed; be aware of regional sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Indian / Native American
rubrics_metrics.description: Both terms are generally acceptable; tribal affiliation is preferred for individuals. Federal recognition criteria differ from self-identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify people by their preferred tribal affiliation; use 'native-born' for someone born in the U.S. but not American Indian. Note federal law updates (HR 4238) and provide census definitions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Sign Language
rubrics_metrics.description: A full language using hand signs, facial expressions, and body posture; many deaf or hard-of-hearing people use ASL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize and spell out on first reference; 'ASL' acceptable on second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1990 federal civil rights law addressing disability discrimination in employment and public accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full name on first reference and 'ADA' thereafter; link to ADA.gov for more information in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amish
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious group descended from Swiss Anabaptists, known for plain dress and rejection of certain technologies; governed by the Ordnung.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cultural and doctrinal context when reporting; use correct terminology for leaders (bishops) and avoid stereotyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: amputation, amputee
rubrics_metrics.description: Amputation refers to removal of an extremity; 'amputee' is acceptable for someone who has undergone amputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'amputee' or 'someone who has had an amputation'; be precise if the condition is not due to amputation but a congenital difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: anchor baby, anchor child
rubrics_metrics.description: Pejorative term for a child born to a noncitizen mother in a country granting birthright citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid except in direct quotations; describe circumstances more accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: androgyne
rubrics_metrics.description: A person whose biological sex is not readily apparent or who is between two genders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for preferred terms and pronouns; cross-reference related gender identity terms.
